repairs.after: {"q": "The kubelet's detection of whether the tmpfs noswap option is available is described as temporary. What would let that logic be removed?", "answer": "Wide support for the option: once the tmpfs noswap option is very widely supported the concern goes away and the detection logic can simply be dropped", "accept": ["wide support; the probe can go away", "wide support; the detection logic is dropped", "wide support; drop the check", "wide support; remove the detection"]}
repairs.rationale: The target is right -- future_cleanup is verbatim in the brief prompt and is the closing sentence of the human span (kep-2400 lines 521-522) -- but every accept string spelled the adjective 'widespread' and the verb 'dropped' in one fixed inflection, and the matcher's lexical test asks whether the key word is a substring of the reply. 'widespread' is not a substring of 'widely'; 'dropped' is not a substring of 'go away'. So the brief's own sentence, run back as a reply, scored 4/8 and failed, and so did the most natural paraphrase. The fix pairs two inflection-proof stems, 'wide' and 'support', with one removal verb per string, and keeps every string at four or five words so the bar rounds to all-or-one-miss. 'wide' matches widely, widespread and wide; 'support' matches supported, supports and support; 'drop' matches dropped and dropping. Verified against five renderings that all now pass: the brief's 'Once support is widespread this probe can go away', the source's own 'when this option would be very widely supported ... hence this logic could be dropped', and the dropped/check/remove variants. Discrimination holds: NOT STATED fails, the stem echo fails, and the two nearest sibling answers -- q4's dummy-mount detection ladder and q1's 'UnlimitedSwap was dropped in beta2', which shares the word 'dropped' -- both fail on the missing 'wide'.

repairs.after: {"q": "Cgroup v1 swap support started out as a goal of this feature. Who concluded it should be abandoned, on what grounds, and what makes the resulting cgroups-v2-only restriction tolerable?", "answer": "sig-node, which concluded that supporting swap there would be very difficult; the restriction is tolerable because that cgroup hierarchy is itself expected to be deprecated eventually, so it should not be a major inconvenience", "accept": ["sig node; too difficult; cgroup deprecate", "sig node; too difficult; cgroup deprecation", "sig node; too hard; cgroup deprecate", "sig node; too hard; cgroup deprecation", "sig node; too difficult; cgroup going away"]}
repairs.rationale: The verify pass was right that nothing was tightened. The string 'cgroup v1' sets numbers_in to {'1'}, the numeric branch runs before the lexical branch, and every string in both the old and the first-repair key contained it, so 'v1', 'There is 1 thing.' and 'cgroup v1 is deprecated.' all scored. The fix removes every digit from the canonical and from all five accept strings, which empties numbers_in and disables the numeric branch entirely; the version numbers stay in the question stem, where they identify the subject without entering the key. Each accept string is a four- or five-word conjunction carrying all three parts the stem asks for: who ('node', which matches both 'sig-node' and 'SIG Node'), the grounds ('difficult' or 'hard'), and the tolerability ('cgroup' plus 'deprecate', 'deprecation' or 'going away'). Both deprecation spellings need their own string because 'deprecate' is a substring of 'deprecated' but not of 'deprecation'. Verified: the three free replies the verify pass demonstrated all fail now, as does NOT STATED and a stem echo. Half answers fail in both directions -- 'sig-node found swap on cgroup v1 too difficult.' misses the tolerability and 'It is acceptable because cgroup v1 will go away.' misses who and the grounds. Four correct renderings pass, including the source's own sentence at kep-2400 lines 502-503, which spells it 'realized ... very difficult' and 'deprecate cgroupv1 eventually'.

unrepaired.why: Vacated when q3 moved from 'which kernel version introduced tmpfs noswap' to future_cleanup, and it should stay vacated: a version number is pure recall, which is why the first pass retargeted it. Nothing else in rfc-06 needs it, and grading it would reopen the numeric hole repaired in q5 -- '6.4' sets numbers_in to {'6.4'}, which is at least specific, but a key built around it scores on the digits alone and measures recall rather than transmission.
